text: A magnet of total magnetic moment $10^{-2}$ $\hat{i}$ $A-m^{2}$ is placed in a time varying magnetic field, B$\hat{i}$ (cos $ωt$)  where B  = 1 Tesla and $ω$ = 0.125 rad/s. The work done for reversing the direction of the magnetic moment at t = 1 second, is -
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the work done in reversing the direction of a magnetic moment in a time-varying magnetic field, we'll follow these steps:

Given:

Magnetic moment: $𝐦=10^{-2}\hat{i}$ A·m²

Magnetic field: $𝐁(t)=B\cos (ωt)\hat{i}$, where $B=1$ T and $ω=0.125$ rad/s

Time at which reversal occurs: $t=1$ s

Step 1: Calculate the Magnetic Field at $t=1$ s

$B(t)=B\cos (ωt)=1\times \cos (0.125\times 1)=\cos (0.125\text{rad})$

Compute $\cos (0.125\text{rad})$:

$\cos (0.125\text{rad})\approx 0.9922$

So,

$B(t)\approx 0.9922\text{T}$

Step 2: Calculate the Work Done

The potential energy $U$ of a magnetic dipole in a magnetic field is:

$U=-𝐦\cdot 𝐁=-mB\cos θ$

The work done $W$ in reversing the magnetic moment from $θ=0^{\circ }$ to $θ=180^{\circ }$ is:

$W=U_{\text{final}}-U_{\text{initial}}=[-mB\cos (180^{\circ })]-[-mB\cos (0^{\circ })]=mB(\cos 0^{\circ }-\cos 180^{\circ })$

Simplify:

$W=mB(1-(-1))=2mB$

Substitute the values:

$W=2\times (10^{-2}\text{A·m}^{2})\times (0.9922\text{T})\approx 0.01984\text{J}$

Step 3: Approximate Using RMS Value

Given that the magnetic field is time-varying, we can consider the root mean square (RMS) value of $\cos (ωt)$ over a complete cycle:

$\text{RMS of}\cos (ωt)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Thus, the RMS value of the magnetic field is:

$B_{\text{RMS}}=B\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=1\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\approx 0.7071\text{T}$

Now, calculate the work done using $B_{\text{RMS}}$:

$W_{\text{RMS}}=2mB_{\text{RMS}}=2\times (10^{-2})\times 0.7071\approx 0.01414\text{J}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot

text: A solid metal cube of edge length 2 cm is moving in a positive y-direction at a constant speed of 6 m/s. There is a uniform magnetic field of 0.1 T in the positive z-direction. The potential difference between the two faces of the cube perpendicular to the x-axis, is -
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We can apply Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction to solve this problem. Faraday's law states that the induced electromotive force (emf) in any closed circuit is equal to the rate of change of the magnetic flux through the circuit.

The cube is moving through a magnetic field, so it's behaving like a conductor moving through a magnetic field. The induced emf or voltage can be calculated by using the formula:

emf = B $\times$ v $\times$ d

Where:

B is the magnetic field strength,

v is the velocity of the conductor, and

d is the length of the conductor perpendicular to the direction of motion and magnetic field.

In this case, the cube is moving in the y-direction and the magnetic field is in the z-direction. So, the faces perpendicular to the x-axis are involved. The length of the conductor (d) perpendicular to the motion and magnetic field is the edge length of the cube, which is 2 cm or 0.02 m.

So, plugging the given values into the formula:

emf = 0.1 T $\times$ 6 m/s $\times$ 0.02 m = 0.012 V = 12 mV

So, the potential difference between the two faces of the cube perpendicular to the x-axis is 12 mV. 

Therefore, Option B is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot

text:

solution.body:
Here given that

density of a material in SI units is $128 kg m^{–3}$

And a new unit system is introduced where 1 unit of length = 25 cm and 1 unit of mass = 50 g

You should know that, physical quantity is same in any unit system. And to calculate a physical quantity you should know two things

(1) numerical value of the physical quantity (n)

(2) unit of the physical quantity (u)

And n $\times$ u = constant in any unit system.

Here in SI unit system,

 $n_{1} = 128$

$u_{1} = kg/m^{3}$

And in new unit system,

$n_{2} =$ ?

$u_{2} = 50gm/(25cm)^{3}$

As $n_{1}u_{1} = n_{2}u_{2}$

$\therefore$ 128 $\times$ $(kg/m^{3}) = n_{2}$ $\times$ $50gm/(25cm)^{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ 128 $\times$ $\frac{1000gm}{(100cm)^{3}}$ $= n_{2}$ $\times$ $\frac{50gm}{(25cm)^{3}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $n_{2} = 128$ $\times$ $\frac{20}{4^{3}}$ = 40

text: A piece of wood of mass 0.03 kg is dropped from the top of a 100 m height building. At the same time, a bullet of mass 0.02 kg is fired vertically upward, with a velocity $100 ms^{–1}$, from the ground. The bullet gets embedded in the wood. Then the maximum height to which the combined system reaches above the top of the building before falling below is $- (g = 10 ms^{–2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Both the wood and the bullet have the same acceleration $g$, so relative to the wood the bullet moves at a constant $100\text{m s}^{-1}$ over the $100\text{m}$ gap. They meet after

$t=\dfrac{100}{100}=1\text{s}$

In this time the wood falls $\dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}=5\text{m}$, so the collision occurs $5\text{m}$ below the top of the building.

Just before the collision the wood ($0.03\text{kg}$) moves down at $gt=10\text{m s}^{-1}$ and the bullet ($0.02\text{kg}$) moves up at $100-gt=90\text{m s}^{-1}$.

The impulse of gravity during the very short collision is negligible, so momentum is conserved (upward positive):

$0.02\times 90-0.03\times 10=0.05v\Rightarrow 1.5=0.05v\Rightarrow v=30\text{m s}^{-1}\text{(upward)}$

The combined body then rises

$h=\dfrac{v^{2}}{2g}=\dfrac{30^{2}}{2\times 10}=45\text{m}$

above the collision point, that is $45-5=40\text{m}$ above the top of the building.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Morning Slot
